Percentage saying crime has gone up 'a little' or 'a lot' in the past few years

column1: Source: Office for National Statistics - Crime Survey for England and Wales

1. A small change to the weighting procedure made in 2019 has been incorporated from the year ending March 2019 and into all historic datasets. The effect of this change will only have a negligible impact on the estimates in this table and therefore not all historic data have been re-calculated using the new weights, except where direct comparisons have been made since January 2019. Years that have been re-calculated using the new weighting procedure are denoted by a 1.

2. From the year ending December 1996 to the year ending December 2000, the questions on the perceptions of national and local crime rates were asked of half the sample. From the year ending March 2002 to the year ending March 2012, these questions were asked of a quarter of the sample.

3. In the year ending March 2009, new questions on the perceptions of national and local crime were introduced into the CSEW. Up to the year ending March 2018, these questions were asked of three quarters of the sample. Since the year ending March 2019 they were asked of half the sample.

4. From year ending March 2009 to year ending March 2012, two questions on perceptions of changing crime levels were included in the CSEW. For year ending March 2013, the question 'How much would you say the crime rate here as changed since two years ago?' was dropped from the survey.
5. Statistically significant change at the 5% level is indicated by an asterisk. For more information on statistical significance, see Chapter 8 of the User Guide.
6. Unweighted base refers to perceived change in national crime. Bases for local crime will be slightly smaller due to only including respondents that have lived in their area 3 years or more.
